childNodes.textContent: As a practical study we ask that 2 small rectangles of the same color and the same size be placed on large grounds of very different color.
Albers' class worked this out by trial and error, with no rules to start from. Pick a part, change its colour, and join the rectangles to check your result. Muted colours change the most.

childNodes.textContent: Soon, these first trials are collected and separated into groups of more and less promise.
Everyone's studies will show here once the site is connected to its database.
A colour changes with its ground. The same grey looks lighter on black than on white
Grounds change a colour in two ways, through light and through hue, and usually both at once
Muted, middle colours change the most. Strong, saturated ones hardly move
Knowing the two rectangles match doesn't stop them looking different
In a UI, a token looks different on every background it sits on, so check colours in place, not on a swatch sheet
